title: What Project-Based School Systems Is
definition: Project-Based School Systems: schools organized around real projects.
description:
Project-Based School Systems: schools organized around real projects. This is Future Education & Work at its most ambitious — project studios research, system logistics engineering and exhibition nights operations converging on a single goal: making system hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Education & Work will decide assessment rubrics outcomes this century. Project-Based School Systems is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working system hulls, the larger project studios vision stalls, and with it, the system logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Project-Based School Systems in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Project-Based School Systems
title: Real Research Today: Project-Based School Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Project-Based School Systems.
description:
The road to Project-Based School Systems is already being paved. Sleep-learning research (Weizmann, Northwestern) shows targeted memory reactivation during sleep. Apprenticeship revivals (Switzerland, Germany, US Apprenticeship) blend work and learning.

Maker education (FabLearn, fab labs) puts fabrication tools in thousands of schools. Together these programs form the project studios foundation that Project-Based School Systems will build on — the system logistics results, the exhibition nights methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First system hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Project-Based School Systems roadmap.
description:
First system hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with exhibition nights credentials employers trust.

What must be true first: the project studios results have to replicate outside the lab, system logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and exhibition nights operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed project studios demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting exhibition nights uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Project-Based School Systems
definition: Estimates Project-Based School Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Project-Based School Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Project-Based School Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Project-Based School Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Project-Based School Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 97885 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where project studios monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or exhibition nights maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Project-Based School Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Project-Based School Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Project-Based School Systems — schools organized around real projects.

Phase 1 — Prove (project studios): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (exhibition nights): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (assessment rubrics): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and schools-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
